_comment: Single source for Merion marketing copy. Consumed by website/src/pages/merion.tsx and web/src/components/merion/*. Every Muse-side row must be stated in docs/merion/MERION.md; rows with no source are left out.
tagline: Your agent gets a real computer. You keep the keys.
lede: Merion gives an untrusted AI agent its own sealed computer on hardware you control, while you hold the policy, the credentials and the approvals. Open source.

values.title: You run it
values.body: A laptop, a mini-PC or your own FluxVM host. Same API everywhere.

values.title: You read it
values.body: Policy is a signed merion.policy.yaml you can diff in git. Apache-2.0.

values.title: You take it with you
values.body: merionctl pack writes your policy, agent manifest and migration notes to a folder. merionctl unpack restores them on another FluxVM node. Secrets are not included.

install.label: Live lab gate
install.note: Needs a FluxVM host and a node22-agent template.

install.label: Move it
install.note: Needs a running agent-runtime and a MERION_EXPORT_TOKEN with scope pack. Secrets are not included.

features.title: Bring your own model
features.body: A model socket. The cell stays the same.

features.title: Signed policy
features.body: Fail-closed Sentinel loaded from a signed YAML file.

features.title: A real cell
features.body: Firecracker/KVM microVM on FluxVM with its own kernel.

features.title: Approvals on your phone
features.body: Buy, send and delete are approved out of band, never in the chat.

features.title: Auto-approve, only if you set it
features.body: Off by default. An operator policy can approve a small, in-policy changeset and journal it; anything outside the policy, or needing a phone signature, still waits for a person.

features.title: Cockpit and browser view
features.body: See taint, recent decisions, tabs, screenshots and a read-only screencast.

features.title: One-click use cases
features.body: PDF brief, contract clauses, security questionnaire, meeting actions, log triage, SBOM summary, CSV cleanup.

features.title: Host network pin
features.body: FluxVM TC/eBPF: deny_udp and gateway-only ports, enforced outside the guest.

features.title: Pack and unpack
features.body: Policy, manifest and migration notes leave as files. Secrets stay in the vault.

compare.label: Where it runs
compare.merion: Your laptop, mini-PC or FluxVM host.

compare.label: Policy
compare.merion: A signed merion.policy.yaml you can diff in git.

compare.label: The cell
compare.muse: Its own dedicated cloud VM; a separate Sentinel on the same machine, kept apart at the system level.
compare.merion: A Firecracker/KVM microVM per cell on FluxVM, with its own kernel; the network policy is applied by the host, outside the guest.

compare.label: Training
compare.merion: Off by default. Export needs a scoped token.

compare.label: Secrets
compare.merion: The same idea: the vault injects on the host, and the agent never sees a real secret.

compare.label: Browser
compare.merion: The same idea: the agent sees structure, you see pixels.

compare.label: Honesty
compare.merion: Up front: measured means software-test until verified hardware.

honesty: Merion runs on measured VMs today, and its evidence class is software-test. Until it runs on verified confidential hardware with a key only you hold, the host can still see inside the VM, and we will not claim otherwise.
